stem.en: A brass alloy contains 70 % copper by mass. How many grams of copper are in 120 g of brass?

explanation.en: 70 % by mass means 70 g of copper in every 100 g of brass. So 120 g of brass holds (70 ÷ 100) × 120 g = 84 g of copper. The rest is zinc: 120 g - 84 g = 36 g. If you got 36 g, you found the zinc, not the copper.

hints.en: How many grams of copper are in 100 g of brass?
Multiply 120 g by 70 and divide by 100.
